terms.gloss: a regular order, the way things follow one another
evidence: Cic. N. D. 2.97: tam ratōs astrōrum ōrdinēs
Cic. Off. 1.17: modum quendam et ōrdinem adhibentēs
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “right order, regular succession”; eundem ōrdinem tenēre, to keep to the same pattern (Cic. Phil. 5.35, Lewis & Short). For patterns of behaviour see practice (custom) and behaviour; for a pattern to copy, model; for a pattern on cloth, design.

evidence: Cic. N. D. 2.125: eaque vicissitūdō in omnī cursū cōnservātur
Cic. Leg. 2.16: vicissitūdinēs diērum noctiumque (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of things that come round in turn: day and night, the seasons, people or birds taking turns.

phrases.latin: Quis enim hunc hominem dīxerit, quī, cum tam certōs caelī mōtūs, tam ratōs astrōrum ōrdinēs … vīderit, neget in hīs ūllam inesse ratiōnem …?
phrases.english: For who would call him a man who, seeing such regular movements in the sky and such fixed patterns in the stars, denies that there is any reason in them?

phrases.latin: in ejus locum succēdit ex hīs, quae adquiērunt, eaque vicissitūdō in omnī cursū cōnservātur
phrases.english: one of those that have rested takes the leader’s place, and this rotation is kept up the whole way (of cranes flying in a wedge)

sources: Lewis & Short: ordo · Lewis & Short: vicissitudo
Cicero, De natura deorum 2 and De officiis 1, checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (9 November 2026).
